mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during similar rate spikes (p > 0.05), or SPX outperforms the S&P 500 5-year risk-free rate spread by more than 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) followed by a subsequent decline strongly predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as market interprets improving labor market conditions.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS shows a double bottom pattern (increase then decrease) over the prior 3 months
failure_condition: No significant excess returns in 60-day window after such labor signal (t-test p > 0.10), or subsequent employment data diverges from the pattern.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% from the prior month coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals expanding economic demand.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth does not predict SPX returns (correlation < 0.2) or 20-day returns are negative during such signals.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two consecutive months triggers a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as expectations of deflation reduce risk premia.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses below 2.0 and remains below for two months
failure_condition: 5-day returns are negative during such deflation signals, or CPIAUCSL recovers rapidly without a sustained break below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in job openings (not in catalog, so use PAYEMS as proxy for labor strength) followed by a sustained drop in unemployment (UNRATE) suggests labor market softening, which precedes a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate wage growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS peaks then UNRATE declines steadily over the next 3 months
failure_condition: No significant positive returns in 60 days after such labor pattern, or UNRATE recovers before the drop completes.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive 2-month decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 200, combined with a rise in industrial production (INDPRO), predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as deflation and supply growth offset each other positively.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 200 for two months AND INDPRO rising trend
failure_condition: No significant return in 20 days during such pattern (p > 0.05), or the interaction coefficient is negative.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent FEDFUNDS above 4%, a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return is expected as markets anticipate higher future policy rates and discount future cash flows more heavily.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are positive during high FEDFUNDS periods (p < 0.05), or FEDFUNDS remains below 4% with similar returns.
